items.readable_text:
Content:
When two angles share a common side, they are called adjacent angles. When two angles are adjacent, we can add their measures to find the measure of the larger angle.

Content:
For example, consider the diagram below.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/c42a6523ca7877948ff78b0c8e8b9cba]

Content:
The angles [MATH: \angle PSR] and [MATH: \angle RST] are adjacent because they both have the side [MATH: \overrightarrow{SR}] in common.

Content:
Since the angles [MATH: \angle PSR] and [MATH: \angle RST] are adjacent, we can find the measure of the combined angle [MATH: \angle PST] by adding the two angles:

Content:
[MATH: m∠PST|= m∠PSR_(⏟)_(orange angle) + m∠RST_(⏟)_(blue angle); = 95^{∘} + 45^{∘}; = 140^{∘}]

We can add the measures of two adjacent angles to find the measure of the combined angle.

Therefore: [MATH: m∠POR|= m∠POQ + m∠QOR; = 68^{∘} + 37^{∘}; = 105^{∘}]

The measure of the angle [MATH: \angle BAD] is [MATH: {90}^{\circ}.] Find the value of [MATH: x.]

[IMG: /graphics/f28c0ea60947bba1747b047ec2c6969f]

sections.normalized_html: EXPLANATION
sections.readable_text: EXPLANATION

sections.normalized_html:
Here, the letter [MATH: x] represents the measure of the unknown angle [MATH: \angle CAD.]

Note the following:

  • The angles [MATH: \angle BAC] and [MATH: \angle CAD] are adjacent because they share the side [MATH: \overrightarrow{AC}.]

  • So, the measure of the large angle [MATH: (\angle BAD)] must be the sum of the measures of the two smaller angles [MATH: (\angle BAC] and [MATH: \angle CAD).]

  • This means that the measure of [MATH: \angle CAD] must be the difference between the large angle [MATH: (\angle BAD)] and the smaller known angle [MATH: (\angle BAC).]

Therefore,

[MATH: x = 90^\circ - 35^\circ = 55^\circ.]

Item 1 — Tutorial: Introduction

Content:
